newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-Britain's CBI sees robust economy in 1997.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Britain's CBI sees robust economy in 1997.

text.p: Britain's biggest business lobby, the Confederation of British Industry (CBI), gave an upbeat assessment of 1997 economic growth on Thursday but warned that interest rates would have to rise to choke off inflation.

But the CBI's monthly industrial trends survey showed demand for finished goods was weaker in December compared with a month earlier as export strength was sapped by the robust climb of the pound this year.

Outlining its economic forecasts for the coming year, the CBI said buoyant consumer spending would boost growth in gross domestic product (GDP) next year to 3.1 percent. Annual GDP growth was 2.4 percent in the third quarter of 1996.
The jump of around 11 percent in the value of the pound since the start of the year has made British goods more expensive to overseas customers.
Sudhir Junankar, the CBI's associate director of economic analysis, said growth could be less robust than the organisation is projecting next year if the pound remains strong.
"I imagine it would take around a quarter percentage point off GDP growth, making it 2.75 percent instead of 3.1 percent," he told a news conference.
The December monthly trends survey showed that while exporters were being hit by the strong pound, demand at home continued to hold up well.
"Demand from overseas has weakened to leave the balance of export order books at their lowest level since February 1994," the CBI said.
Junankar added: "Home demand for manufactured goods continues to hold up and companies remain fairly confident about expanding output over the coming months."

Joining the chorus of British economists who predict interest rate rises next year, the CBI said it expected official rates to rise in several stages to 6.5 percent in the second half of 1997 from 6.0 percent at present.
"If consumer spending rises in line with our forecast, this may put upward pressure on underlying inflation over the next two years," CBI chief economist Kate Barker said.
"With competitive pressures likely to remain intense, we consider that only modest upward moves in interest rates will be sufficient to contain inflation."
Official data released on Thursday showed underlying inflation stuck fast at 3.3 percent in the year to November, well above the government target of 2.5 percent.
Interest rates were left unchanged at the monthly monetary policy meeting between Chancellor of the Exchequer (finance minister) Kenneth Clarke and Bank of England Governor Eddie George on Wednesday.
However, George has said further rate rises will be needed to contain inflationary pressures.

The CBI said strong economic growth should help to bring down unemployment to around 1.7 million by the end of 1997 from 2.03 million in October, the latest month for which official figures are available.
